messages:
elaine: quick heads-up — PR <https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4789|#4789> updates eviction/prefetch TTL handling and adds a tiny migration. I need runtime + platform + security eyes before merge. tl;dr: change default prefetch_ttl from 60 -> 300s, add backfill job to avoid cold starts.
ben: can you paste the diff for the config change? also is this going to change any customer-visible behavior?
elaine: diff snippet:```yaml
services:
  prefetch:
    default_ttl: 300  # was 60
    backfill: true
```
No customer API changes, just defaults for internal cache lifetimes. Customers with pinned configs unaffected.
kai: quick perf q: how did this affect median tail latency in local load tests? any extra mem usage?
elaine: ran a 30m load with seq len 512, continuous batching on 8 GPUs: median gen latency +3ms, p95 +8ms. Memory increased ~40MB per worker due to the prefetch buffer. I can post logs if useful.
morgan: from sec: does the backfill job access any customer creds or KMS? plus need an audit event for when backfill runs.
elaine: no creds touched — backfill reads model keys/pointers only (no plaintext). I'll add an audit entry and a KMS access note in the migration script.
infra-bot: CI: unit ✅, integration ❌ (flake: test_eviction_scheduler::test_race_condition). rerun requested.
ben: I can take a look at the scheduler test tonight, might be flaky under the new timing. if infra-bot still fails, ping me.
kai: also suggest a canary rollout (10% of requests) and keep an automatic rollback if p95 goes up >15% for 10m. can we add that to the rollout plan?
elaine: yup — I'll attach a canary plan to the PR with those thresholds and owner (ben) for rollback.
morgan: add a short note in the PR about audit events and confirm no new network egress. then sec is happy to approve.
ben: grabbing the test now, will post a quick fix if I find a timing window. ETA ~3h.
elaine: great — thanks all. I'll hold merge until we have runtime + sec LGTMs and CI green. ping me if you need any logs or replay data. :thumbsup:
